| **Likelihood** | possible — A moral prescription rather than a forecast; it needs firms and governments to put human agency ahead of cost-cutting, while current deployment leans towards cost savings. |
| **Assessed** | 2026-11-27 |

AI can relieve people of repetitive tasks and support human judgement. Its use at work should preserve meaningful employment and human responsibility. Deploying it chiefly to cut costs risks displacement, tighter monitoring and greater inequality.

| Reliable safety net | 3 | Not addressed in the extract. |
| Responsive government | 3 | Subsidiarity and human responsibility are defended against concentrated control and surveillance, but no new mechanism is proposed (§§47, 52–55). |
| Time for what matters | 4 | The section is not addressed, but the scenario assumes meaningful relationships are preserved and warns against simulated companionship in care and schooling (§§56–63, 71–74). |
